events.continuity_hook: The lodging room arrangement is settled and the outbound trip is unchanged; only the retimed return journey and any resulting car or hotel extension remain unresolved.
events.interaction_goal: Verify whether the 34-minute connection is valid and realistically usable, compare the later same-day and next-morning alternatives in full, and confirm the revised return itinerary without disturbing the outbound reservations.
events.scenario_brief: Nine days before the Monterey Peninsula trip, the airline moves the San Jose return connection 55 minutes earlier, leaving only 34 minutes at the connecting airport. Maya and her partner can accept that itinerary, move to a later connection that reaches Minneapolis at 11:40 p.m., or switch both return segments to the next morning for an added $176 total. The inn and rental car can each be extended one night, but their combined added cost would be $264.

events.continuity_hook: This opens a new two-day client episode with fixed workshop hours, separate travel limits, and unresolved flights, lodging, and airport-to-office transportation.
events.interaction_goal: Map feasible Monday outbound and Wednesday return windows, estimate the complete cost of an office-area and airport-area structure, and identify a practical plan before individual reservations are selected.
events.scenario_brief: Maya is assigned to lead a client configuration workshop in Dublin, Ohio, from 8:30 a.m. Tuesday through 3:30 p.m. Wednesday. She can leave Minneapolis after 2:00 p.m. Monday and needs to return Wednesday night. Airfare is capped at $760, lodging at $245 per night before tax, and local transportation is reimbursable separately. No reservations exist, and the first search must determine whether staying near the client office or near Columbus airport produces the more workable trip.

events.continuity_hook: The trip will use a hotel near the client office, so the flight decision now determines Monday check-in time and whether Wednesday's workshop can be attended in full.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the flight timelines and fares, reject any option that conflicts with the workshop, account for airport transfer time in both directions, and select an itinerary within the air limit.
events.scenario_brief: The office-area structure is leading. A $552 nonstop reaches Columbus at 6:50 p.m. Monday and returns at 7:05 p.m. Wednesday, while a $436 connecting itinerary arrives at 9:35 p.m. and has a 46-minute connection on the return. A third combination costs $621 and provides an earlier Wednesday departure, but it requires Maya to leave the workshop before the scheduled close.

events.continuity_hook: Air travel is fixed, and lodging must now fit the Monday arrival, the two workshop mornings, and the Wednesday airport transfer.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate the two-night totals after tax, compare check-in and transportation details, verify that the client-rate property can hold a late arrival, and choose the hotel that stays within the nightly limit.
events.scenario_brief: The nonstop flights have been selected, requiring two hotel nights. A client-rate property two blocks from the workshop costs $231 nightly before tax and includes breakfast, but its Monday front desk closes at 10:00 p.m. A second hotel costs $204 nightly, has round-the-clock check-in, and is 12 minutes away by rideshare. A third costs $238 nightly and includes an airport shuttle, though the shuttle stops running before Wednesday's planned airport departure.

events.continuity_hook: All trip components have been selected, with purchase timing, late-arrival notation, and the final chronological itinerary left to confirm.
events.interaction_goal: Reconcile the fare, lodging, and local transportation estimate, verify each date and time, record the hotel arrival note, and complete the flight and room reservations in deadline order.
events.scenario_brief: Maya has chosen the $552 nonstop airfare and the client-rate hotel, totaling $526 after tax for two nights. Estimated round-trip rideshare costs add $94, bringing the trip estimate to $1,172. The airfare hold expires at 7:30 p.m.; the hotel can note an arrival after 8:00 p.m. and remains cancellable until 6:00 p.m. the day before check-in.

events.continuity_hook: The hotel, workshop, and Wednesday return remain intact, but the canceled outbound flight requires same-day replacement travel and an updated arrival plan.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the replacement flights by total out-of-pocket cost, arrival reliability, connection risk, and hotel timing; secure the stronger option; and update the airport transfer and late check-in details.
events.scenario_brief: On Monday afternoon, Maya's nonstop to Columbus is canceled before she leaves for the airport. The airline offers a 6:20 p.m. connecting itinerary arriving at 10:48 p.m., while another carrier has a $689 nonstop arriving at 9:15 p.m. with no transfer of the original ticket value. The hotel will hold the room until midnight if contacted, and both alternatives still allow arrival before Tuesday's 8:30 a.m. workshop.
